finding.statement: The younger Berkhamsted John was opened as a candidate on a departure-shaped gap in the record, and that gap does not exist. His household's last baptism is Francis in 1636/7; within the following two years the parish buried Joane (November 1637), Richard (June 1638), William (October 1638), Elizabeth (February 1638/9) and Francis (March 1638/9), and two of those are demonstrably his own children. A household that loses four or five members in eighteen months and then stops appearing in the baptism register is displaying mortality, not departure. The finding matters beyond this candidate: a departure-shaped gap is only evidence where the burial series for the same parish and window has been read and shown to be covered.

finding.statement: Great Berkhamsted's burial register survives, is transcribed, and holds sixteen Gurney-variant burials between 1579 and 1643: Jhone Gernnye 1579; Isabell Gourney 1601; Henry Gourney 1607; Jhon Gourney 1612; Jhon Gourney 1620; Thomas Gorne 1620; Joane Gurney 7 November 1637; Richard Gurney 28 June 1638; William Gurney 1 October 1638; Elizabeth Gurney 21 February 1638/9; Francis Gurney 9 March 1638/9; Thomas Gurney 1639 (two rows); Margaret Gurney 1643; and Thomas Gurney 1643. Five fall between November 1637 and March 1638/9. Two of those five - Elizabeth, baptised 2 August 1629, and Francis, baptised 1 March 1636/7 - match to the day the death dates independently recorded for two children of the younger John Gurney, on two providers and two record classes. The parish is distinct from Little Berkhamstead twenty miles east, which the same place keyword also matches and which carries no Gurney entry in this window.
